2027-06-02.title: Wednesday of the second week after Pentecost
readings: The message about the cross: foolishness to some, the power of God to us
The kingdom of God is like a mustard seed and like yeast
2027-06-02.alt: Season of Pentecost, the week after the Second Sunday after Pentecost. No commemoration is printed in the Panchangam (Panchangam 2026–27, p. 56).
2027-06-02.verse: For the message about the cross is foolishness to those who are perishing, but to us who are being saved it is the power of God.
theo: In the first week of June the farmers of Kerala watch the sky. When the monsoon breaks, they plant: paddy seedlings in the flooded fields, pepper cuttings at the foot of the trees, tapioca stems in the wet red earth. Nothing looks less impressive than a stick pushed into mud. Yet a few months later there is a harvest. Today's readings speak of God's way of working, which is very like the farmer's in June: small, hidden, apparently foolish, and in the end astonishingly fruitful. St Paul begins with the hardest example of all: “For the message about the cross is foolishness to those who are perishing, but to us who are being saved it is the power of God.” To the educated people of Corinth, a city proud of its orators and its schools, a crucified Jew from Galilee was not a message of salvation but a scandal. The cross was the punishment for slaves and rebels, a thing one did not mention in polite company. And Paul builds everything on it.

He knows the objections and names them: “For Jews demand signs and Greeks desire wisdom, but we proclaim Christ crucified, a stumbling block to Jews and foolishness to Gentiles, but to those who are the called, both Jews and Greeks, Christ the power of God and the wisdom of God.” Paul is himself a Jew, and he is not mocking anyone; he is describing two honest human hungers, the hunger for a mighty deed and the hunger for a convincing argument, and saying that God has answered both in a way no one expected. The sign is the Son of God dying out of love; the wisdom is the plan of the Father to save the world through weakness. “For God's foolishness is wiser than human wisdom, and God's weakness is stronger than human strength.” St John Chrysostom, preaching on this passage, marvelled that twelve unlettered fishermen, armed only with the message of a crucified man, had persuaded the cities and the philosophers of the world; he said that this itself was the greatest proof that the Cross is the power of God (Homilies on 1 Corinthians 4, in substance). We who make the sign of the Cross so easily, on our foreheads, over our food, over our children at night, should remember what a bold thing it is: we are signing ourselves with God's foolishness and declaring that it is wiser than anything the world can offer.

In the Gospel Jesus gives two small pictures of the same truth. “What is the kingdom of God like? And to what should I compare it? It is like a mustard seed that someone took and sowed in the garden; it grew and became a tree, and the birds of the air made nests in its branches.” And again: “It is like yeast that a woman took and mixed in with three measures of flour until all of it was leavened.” The mustard seed was proverbial among the Jews for smallness. Three measures of flour was a very large amount, enough to feed a whole household and its guests, and a little yeast, hidden inside it, changes all of it. Neither the seed nor the yeast makes any noise. Both work from within and both take time. This is how the Holy Spirit, poured out at Pentecost, works in the Church and in each of us: through a word of Scripture that stays in the heart, through a Holy Qurbono attended faithfully on an ordinary weekday, through a small act of kindness that nobody sees. We grow impatient and want quick results, big crowds, visible success. The Lord asks us to plant and to knead, and to trust him for the growth. As the rains come down on the fields this week, let us ask him to let the seed of his word fall into our hearts and to let the yeast of the Gospel work quietly through our homes and our parish.
outline: Ask: do I trust small and hidden things to be the way God works?
Point 1 · The foolishness of the cross
What the world calls weakness is the power of God.
The smallest beginning becomes a tree with room for the birds.
Point 3 · The yeast in the flour
The Gospel works quietly from within until all is changed.
“To us who are being saved it is the power of God.”
live: Sign yourself with the cross (1 Corinthians 1:18)
Make the sign of the Cross slowly and deliberately three times today, remembering that it is the power of God.
Do one small, hidden good deed today and tell no one about it.
2027-06-02.prayer: Lord Jesus Christ, crucified and risen, you are the power of God and the wisdom of God. When the world laughs at the message of your Cross, keep us faithful to it; when we look for great signs and clever words, turn our eyes back to your love poured out for us. Make your kingdom grow in us like the mustard seed and work in us like yeast hidden in the flour. Bless the rains that fall on our fields in these days and the seed that our farmers sow. You live and reign with the Father and the Holy Spirit, for ever. Amen.
altar: In the Holy Qurbono the foolishness of the Cross is made present: the one sacrifice of Christ is offered on the altar under the humble signs of bread and wine. Nothing looks smaller than a piece of bread, and nothing is greater than what it becomes.

quick: To those who are perishing the message of the cross is foolishness; to those being saved it is the power of God.
Christ crucified is the power of God and the wisdom of God; God's foolishness is wiser than human wisdom.
The kingdom of God is like a mustard seed that grows into a tree and like yeast that leavens a great mass of flour.
2027-06-02.action: Do one small good deed in secret today and leave the growth to God.
2027-06-02.question: Where am I impatient for quick, visible results instead of trusting God's hidden way of working?

family.explain: Jesus told two little stories. A mustard seed is tiny, smaller than a grain of rice, but it grows into a big plant where birds can build nests. A little yeast mixed into a big bowl of flour makes the whole dough rise, like the dough for appam. God's kingdom grows like that: from small beginnings, quietly, from inside. Every small kind thing we do is like a seed or a pinch of yeast.
family.intention: We pray for our farmers who are planting in this rainy season, and for every small good work in our family to grow.
family.ask: Ask: “What is one small seed of kindness I can plant tomorrow?”

illus: In a village near Kollam, a widow began in the 1990s to keep a few rupees aside every week in a tin on her kitchen shelf. When the tin was full she would buy notebooks and pencils for one child in the colony who could not afford them. She never spoke about it. Years later, at her funeral, the parish priest was surprised to see a group of young men and women he did not know standing near the back: a nurse, two teachers, an engineer, a police constable. They had all, as children, received their first notebooks from her tin. One of them said: it was such a small thing; it was the reason I stayed in school. The priest went home and read again the parable of the mustard seed.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, your Cross is the power of God. Sow your word in our hearts like a seed and let it grow, quietly and surely, by your Spirit. Amen.
share: For the message about the cross is foolishness to those who are perishing, but to us who are being saved it is the power of God (1 Corinthians 1:18). When has the Cross been power for me?
It is like a mustard seed that someone took and sowed in the garden; it grew and became a tree (Luke 13:19). What small beginning in my life did God make grow?
It is like yeast that a woman took and mixed in with three measures of flour until all of it was leavened (Luke 13:21). Where can I be a little yeast this week?
pm.resp: Lord, let your kingdom grow in us.
interc: For the Church, that she may proclaim Christ crucified with courage, even when the world calls it foolishness.
For preachers and teachers of the faith, that they may trust the power of the Cross more than their own cleverness.
For our farmers and all who work the land in this monsoon season, that their sowing may be blessed.
For all who feel that their good efforts are too small to matter, that they may be encouraged.
For our parish, that the Gospel may work in us like yeast, quietly changing our homes and our town.
pm.close: Father, in the foolishness of the Cross you have shown your wisdom, and in small seeds you prepare a great harvest. Give us faith to trust your hidden ways and patience to wait for your growth. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

homily: Dear friends, in these days the monsoon has come and our farmers are planting. A seedling in the mud does not look like much. But they plant in hope, because they know what will come. Today God's word tells us that he works the same way.

St Paul says: For the message about the cross is foolishness to those who are perishing, but to us who are being saved it is the power of God (1 Corinthians 1:18). Some people wanted miracles, others wanted clever arguments. God gave the world something nobody expected: his Son dying on a cross out of love. For God's foolishness is wiser than human wisdom, and God's weakness is stronger than human strength (1 Corinthians 1:25).

Jesus gives two pictures. The kingdom of God is like a mustard seed that someone took and sowed in the garden; it grew and became a tree (Luke 13:19). And it is like yeast that a woman took and mixed in with three measures of flour until all of it was leavened (Luke 13:21). The seed is tiny; the yeast is hidden. But they change everything, slowly, from inside.

So let us not despise small things. A prayer said every night, a Holy Qurbono on a weekday, a kind word, a small gift to the poor: these are seeds and yeast. We plant; God gives the growth. And let us make the sign of the Cross with faith, because the Cross, which looks like weakness, is the power of God. Amen.
kids: Children, have you ever planted a seed? You put a tiny seed into the soil, you water it, and you wait. One day a little green shoot comes up! Jesus said God's kingdom is like a tiny mustard seed that grows into a big plant where birds make their nests. Every time you say a prayer, share your snack, or help your mother, you are planting a little seed for God. Do not worry if it is small. God will make it grow.

intro: Theme: “For the message about the cross is foolishness to those who are perishing, but to us who are being saved it is the power of God.”
On Wednesday of the second week after Pentecost, in the season of monsoon sowing: the foolishness of the Cross, the mustard seed and the yeast, and God's small and hidden ways.

sub: Signs and wisdom: two honest hungers.
God answers both in Christ crucified.
Twelve fishermen and the cities of the world.
q: For my thoughts are not your thoughts, nor are your ways my ways, says the Lord.
May I never boast of anything except the cross of our Lord Jesus Christ, by which the world has been crucified to me, and I to the world.
points.apply: Put a small cross where you will see it at your desk or in your shop, and look at it when you are tempted to trust only in cleverness or money.

sub: Room in its branches for the birds.
q: On the mountain height of Israel I will plant it, in order that it may produce boughs and bear fruit, and become a noble cedar. Under it every kind of bird will live; in the shade of its branches will nest winged creatures of every kind.
I planted, Apollos watered, but God gave the growth.
points.apply: Begin one small, regular good practice this week (a daily decade of the Rosary, a weekly visit to a lonely person) and keep it up.

sub: A Christian in an office, a classroom, a family.
q: For whoever has despised the day of small things shall rejoice
In the same way, let your light shine before others, so that they may see your good works and give glory to your Father in heaven.
points.apply: Choose one place where you spend much time (work, school, a WhatsApp group) and be quietly kind and honest there all this week.

concl: God works like a farmer in June: he plants what looks small and foolish, and waits for the harvest.
The Cross, the seed and the yeast all say the same thing: trust his hidden power.
2027-06-02.resolve: Do not despise small things: plant, knead, and leave the growth to God.
